title: On truncations of hierarchical equations of motion for finite-dimensional systems: spectral convergence of the truncated Liouvillians (Theorem 2)
author: Vasilii Vadimov
work: On truncations of hierarchical equations of motion for finite-dimensional systems
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's spectral convergence theorem for truncated Liouvillians, printed as Theorem 2 (Spectral convergence) at source0.tex lines 688-702 and delivered with the paper's own complete 153-line proof (lines 704-856). The statement is that for every compact spectral region K and every exhausting sequence of truncations, once the truncation is deep enough each chosen neighbourhood of a spectral value contains eigenvalues of the truncated Liouvillian with exactly the matching algebraic multiplicity, and no truncated eigenvalues lie outside those neighbourhoods. The proof is a source-local argument that has to be assembled rather than quoted: it bounds the resolvent of the exact Liouvillian on the boundaries of the chosen neighbourhoods and on the complementary compact set, uses the retained Schur-complement convergence lemma to make the truncation error smaller than the reciprocal of that bound, follows the eigenvalues through the homotopy z - L - t(L_trunc - L), applies the argument principle to count eigenvalues inside each contour, and then proves invertibility of the truncated operator on the complement by a Neumann-series estimate of the Schur complement. No qualifying examination poses a spectral convergence theorem for truncated Liouvillians with multiplicity matching and a contour argument under a Schur-complement perturbation bound; the unit is H2.
